name: Disorder of Amino Acid and Other Organic Acid Metabolism

ethnicAssociations: Certain populations with founder mutations (e.g., Ashkenazi Jews, Amish)

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Biochemical and Molecular Diagnostic Criteria for Organic Acidurias and Aminoacidopathies

criteria.description: Detection of abnormal levels of amino acids or organic acids in blood or urine by chromatography or mass spectrometry
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in amino acid or organic acid metabolism
Presence of characteristic clinical manifestations such as metabolic acidosis, developmental delay, or neurological symptoms
Positive family history of similar metabolic disorders or consanguinity
Improvement of symptoms with dietary management or cofactor supplementation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Abnormal biochemical profile plus genetic confirmation or characteristic clinical features with biochemical evidence
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Early diagnosis is critical to prevent irreversible neurological damage.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Metabolic ketoacidosis with elevated organic acids

searchTerms: severe newborn brain dysfunction with low muscle tone

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hyperammonemia secondary to organic acid accumulation
searchTerms: high ammonia levels from organic acid buildup

laboratory: Elevated plasma amino acids or abnormal amino acid profile
Increased urinary organic acids detected by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry
Metabolic acidosis with elevated anion gap
imaging: Brain MRI showing white matter abnormalities or basal ganglia lesions
Echocardiogram demonstrating cardiomyopathy in some cases
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes encoding enzymes of amino acid or organic acid metabolism (e.g., PAH, MCCC1, ACADS)
other: Abnormal newborn screening results for amino acid or organic acid disorders

distinguishingFeatures: Marked hyperammonemia without significant organic acid elevation
Normal amino acid profile except for elevated glutamine
Variable genetic mutations affecting mitochondrial DNA or nuclear genes

redFlags: Rapid onset of encephalopathy in neonate or infant
Severe metabolic acidosis refractory to standard treatment
Progressive neurological deterioration despite supportive care
references: Saudubray JM, Garcia-Cazorla A. Inborn errors of metabolism overview: pathophysiology, manifestations, evaluation, and management. Pediatr Clin North Am. 2018;65(2):179-208.
